headline: Sales edge higher while profit and margins surge
summary_short: AYI's Q3 FY2026 (fiscal period FY2026 Q2 on our calendar) net sales rose 1.6% y/y to $1,198M as Acuity Intelligent Spaces growth offset a lighting-segment dip, while GAAP operating profit jumped 38.3% and diluted EPS rose 46.2% to $4.56 on the absence of year-ago special charges and a lower share count.
summary_long: Net sales rose 1.6% y/y to $1,198M (+13.5% q/q) as 14.9% growth in Acuity Intelligent Spaces offset a 1.9% decline in Acuity Brands Lighting. GAAP operating margin expanded 420bp y/y to 16.1%, largely because the year-ago quarter carried $29.7M of special charges and $19.2M of acquired-inventory profit drag that did not recur; adjusted operating profit grew a more modest 0.8%. Diluted EPS rose 46.2% to $4.56 (adjusted diluted EPS +3.7% to $5.31), helped by a roughly 1.9% lower diluted share count from ongoing buybacks (about $230M repurchased year-to-date). Nine-month operating cash flow was $520.2M and free cash flow $461.7M. No forward guidance was disclosed in the release.

drivers.explanation: Management framed the quarter as solid execution: sales growth, higher adjusted operating profit, higher adjusted diluted EPS and strong cash flow with effective capital allocation.
Acuity Intelligent Spaces sales grew 14.9% on connected-building and audio/video/control strength, offsetting a 1.9% Acuity Brands Lighting decline led by a weaker direct sales network.
Cost of products sold fell 2.8% y/y as a richer mix from faster-growing, higher-margin AIS offset ABL's revenue decline; q/q cost rose in line with higher sequential volume.
Gross margin expanded 220bp y/y as AIS's much higher segment gross margin (60.3% vs ABL's 46.8%) grew faster than ABL, aided by $6.4M of tariff refunds.
Same mix-shift and tariff-refund dynamics as the gross-profit driver above, expressed as a margin rather than a dollar figure.
GAAP operating profit jumped 38.3% mainly because the year-ago quarter absorbed $29.7M of special charges and $19.2M of acquired-inventory profit drag that did not recur.
420bp of expansion mirrors the operating-income driver: absence of prior-year special charges and acquisition-related cost drag, per the non-GAAP reconciliation table.
Moves in line with GAAP operating income this quarter; the two figures sit within $0.3M of each other.
EBITDA growth outpaced EBIT as depreciation and amortization stayed elevated on acquisition-related intangible amortization, so most of the EBIT gain carried through.
Benefited from the operating-profit gain plus lower interest expense ($6.1M vs $12.1M) on reduced average debt after term-loan repayments.
Tracked the pretax-income gain; the effective tax rate ticked up slightly, but profit growth was still dominated by the operating-line improvement.
Margin gained 350bp y/y as net income grew far faster than the modest sales increase, per the reconciliation table's own percent-of-sales lines.
Basic EPS rose in line with diluted EPS on the same profit growth and a lower weighted share count.
Diluted EPS growth (46.2%) outpaced net income growth (43.3%) as the diluted share count fell about 1.9% y/y on ongoing buybacks.
Acuity repurchased about 766,000 shares year-to-date for roughly $230 million under its ongoing share-repurchase program.
